messages:
laura: Heads-up — onboarding report: user hit a fncall JSON-mode failure when schema had nullable arrays.
laura: repro steps attached below.

mike: ok can you paste the minimal prompt + schema?

laura: sure — snippet: 
```json
{"tool": "search","input": {"query": "cats","filters": null}}
```
and schema expected `filters` to be `array<string> | null` but SDK helper coerced null -> [] on node only.

jason: we ran into a parity thing last week. Node SDK's JSON-mode helper runs a `coerceEmpty()` pass that turns nullish to empty arrays to avoid downstream code failing. Python leaves null.

sam: that's nasty for onboarding because customers assume strict schema validation from the model. Do we want the helper to preserve nulls and let schema validation surface errors instead?

mike: ideally parity. Which is more common in user schemas? nullable array or optional field?

laura: in sample apps we have both. The problem manifested because auth/retry wrapper retried the fncall and double-coerced on the second pass — result became `[[]]` in some cases. Crashy.

jason: reproduction: initial model output `{"filters": null}` -> node helper converts to `[]` -> retry wrapper wraps payload and helper runs again on already-coerced value (bug) -> becomes `[[]]`.

sam: @ci-bot can we get a quick unit test in the SDK suite showing idempotence for helpers?

ci-bot: ci-bot: created ticket DE-4921 and a flaky test job. Link: https://ci.redwood/DE-4921

mike: proposed fix: make the helper pure and run only on raw model string parse, not on objects already passed through helpers. Add a guard `if (_alreadyNormalized) return obj;` or better, make normalization a single step in the JSON-mode parser.

laura: also need a migration note in onboarding docs — mention Node vs Py parity gap and show recommended schema patterns (prefer `[]` vs `null`?)

sam: I'd argue docs should recommend explicit nullability and include a snippet: 
```yaml
properties:
  filters:
    type: ["array", "null"]
    items:
      type: "string"
```

jason: I'll open a PR to remove the double-run and add tests. Will also add a sampleapp example that triggers the earlier bug so QE can catch regressions.

laura: thanks — ping me when PR is up, I'll add to the onboarding checklist so SRE/customer success know. :thumbsup:

mike: filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/834 — adds idempotent normalize, unit test, and docs note.

sam: awesome. follow-up: can we add a small lint rule in the samplekit that warns if schema uses array|null and code expects array? Might save a lot of friction.

jason: noted. I'll prototype a schema-lint rule in samplekit.

laura: closing loop — thanks everyone.
